results.title: How invoicing works - Stripe Documentation
results.content:
### Uncollectible invoice status and transitions

> “uncollectible | The customer is unlikely to pay the invoice. Normally, you treat it as bad debt in your accounting process. | - Change the invoice’s status to `void` or `paid`.”

> “Optionally, you can change the status of an unpaid invoice to `void` or `uncollectible`.”

> “You can only void an invoice in `open` or `uncollectible` status.”

> “As a result, you decide to write off the invoice as unlikely to be paid. In this case, you can update the status of the invoice to be `uncollectible`. This allows you to track the amount owed for reporting purposes as part of your bad debt accounting process.”

> “You can mark an open invoice as uncollectible in the Dashboard.”

> “To mark an open invoice as uncollectible using the API, use the Mark uncollectible endpoint…”

> “If you’ve configured webhook endpoints, you’ll receive a `invoice.marked_uncollectible` event when an invoice moves into the `uncollectible` status.”

### Relevant status table rows

| Status | Description | Possible actions |
|---|---|---|
| `void` | “This invoice is canceled.” | “No further actions.” |
| `uncollectible` | “The customer is unlikely to pay the invoice. Normally, you treat it as bad debt in your accounting process.” | “Change the invoice’s status to `void` or `paid`.” |

### Subscriptions and invoice generation

> “*Subscriptions* (A Subscription represents the product details associated with the plan that your customer subscribes to. Allows you to charge the customer on a recurring basis) automatically generate invoices for each billing cycle.”

The page does **not** state whether a subscription becomes active when an invoice is voided or marked uncollectible, or whether unpaid subscriptions continue to generate invoices.

results.title: Pay an invoice | Stripe API Reference
results.content:
The page does not state what happens when an uncollectible invoice is paid or voided, whether an invoice can transition from uncollectible to paid, whether a subscription becomes active when an invoice is voided or marked uncollectible, or whether unpaid subscriptions continue to generate invoices.

Relevant fields in the example response:

| Field | Exact value |
|---|---|
| `status` | `"paid"` |
| `status_transitions.finalized_at` | `1680641304` |
| `status_transitions.marked_uncollectible_at` | `null` |
| `status_transitions.paid_at` | `1680641304` |
| `status_transitions.voided_at` | `null` |

The page states: “Stripe automatically creates and then attempts to collect payment on invoices for customers on subscriptions according to your subscriptions settings.”

results.title: How subscriptions work
results.content:
### Exact statements about uncollectible and voided invoices

> “To settle an invoice, pay it, void it, or manually mark it uncollectible.”

> “An invoice that Stripe marks uncollectible after ending payment retries remains outstanding.”

> “To identify blocking invoices, [list the subscription’s invoices](https://docs.stripe.com/api/invoices/list.md) with a status of `open` or `uncollectible`. An uncollectible invoice remains outstanding only when its reason is `max_payment_attempts` or `payment_not_received`. Other reasons, such as `user_forgiven`, don’t block the subscription from becoming active.”

> “Voided invoices don’t affect subscription status.”

The page does **not** explicitly state that an invoice transitions from `uncollectible` to `paid`, or from `uncollectible` to `void`. It does state that an invoice can be settled by paying it, voiding it, or manually marking it uncollectible.

### Relevant subscription-status table statements

| Status | Exact statement |
|---|---|
| `active` | “Your [subscription settings](https://dashboard.stripe.com/settings/billing/subscriptions#manage-failed-payments) determine which invoices must be settled to transition a `past_due` subscription to `active`. When status resolution uses the most recent invoice, Stripe uses the most recent non-voided invoice to determine the subscription’s status. Paying that invoice or manually marking it as uncollectible transitions the subscription to `active`. When status resolution uses all invoices, settle all applicable outstanding invoices to transition the subscription to `active`.” |
| `active` | “When status resolution uses the most recent invoice, you can leave other outstanding invoices open for payment, mark them as uncollectible or void them as you see fit.” |
| `past_due` | “To reactivate the subscription, pay the most recent non-voided invoice or manually mark it as uncollectible when status resolution uses the most recent invoice, or settle applicable outstanding invoices when status resolution uses all invoices. The subscription becomes `active` regardless of whether you settle the required invoices before or after their due dates.” |
| `unpaid` | “To move the subscription to `active`, pay the most recent non-voided invoice or manually mark it as uncollectible when status resolution uses the most recent invoice, or settle applicable outstanding invoices when status resolution uses all invoices.” |

### Whether unpaid subscriptions continue generating invoices

> “The subscription continues to generate invoices but doesn’t attempt payment.”

The page also states:

> “If the customer doesn’t pay a subscription invoice, Stripe pauses further collection attempts. The subscription continues to generate invoices each billing period, which remain in `draft` status.”
